Cursor's AI support agent hallucinated a single-device login policy, telling a user this was intentional. A Cursor developer later clarified: 'We have no such policy... this is an incorrect response from a front-line AI support bot.' The false answer triggered public subscription cancellations and a viral Reddit thread.

"Cursor is weird. They have a basically unused GitHub with a thousand unanswered Issues. It's so buggy in ways that VSCode isn't. I hate it. Also I use it everyday and pay for it. That's when you know you've captured something, when people hate use your product."
A user considering alternatives said they tried Continue but were unimpressed with tab completion and typing experience, describing it as 'laggy typing on a remote server.'
"Sadly, Cursor will always be hampered by maintaining its own VSCode fork. Others in this niche are expanding rapidly and I, myself, have started transitioning to using Roo and Cline."
Cursor is caught in a cat-and-mouse game against workarounds where users create new accounts to get unlimited use; a repo enabling this (cursor-free-vip) was trending on GitHub.
"I just cancelled - not because I thought the policy change was real - but simply because this article reminded me I hadn't used it much this month."

A commenter noted only about 4 users in the thread actually claimed they would cancel subscriptions over the fake policy, and most hedged their statements, casting doubt on claims of mass cancellations.
"That's a lot of money for a buggy product that is at best slightly better than its competitors."
"Cursor is an extension for VS Code, a harness and a bunch of prompts. They have their own model (Composer 2) which is based on Kimi K2.5, but I don't think SpaceX would be interested in it."
"Not bad for a VS Code fork and a Chinese LLM fine tune."
A commenter pointed out that Claude Code and Codex are 'chipping away at Cursor very hard,' questioning what strategic advantage the acquisition provides.
"I once again fear for my grandfathered-in free SuperMaven," referencing a competing tab-completion tool users still preferred to keep alongside/instead of Cursor.
